clue.text: Computer in theory chiming strangely with nature

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of the two words that follow are arranged in an odd new order

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a theoretical computer would chime oddly with the natural world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges the thirteen letters of CHIMING and NATURE; 'with' just joins the two fodder words.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan Turing's abstract machine is the theoretical model of a computer, existing on paper rather than in hardware.

clue.text: One being shelled in bad mood?

definitions.meaning: a creature that gets taken out of its shell before eating, or that wears a hard shell
crabbiness: in old usage a ... is a fit of sour temper, as in being crabby

explanation.surface: A soldier under artillery fire is understandably grumpy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shelled' suggests bombardment, but it is the shellfish having its shell cracked open; 'in' only links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The crustacean is shelled at the table, and crabbed or crabby temper gives the second, grumpy sense.

clue.text: A gesture to reform unpredictable administration

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so the letters of the preceding three words are put into a new shape

explanation.surface: A politician proposes a gesture aimed at reforming an erratic government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' rearranges A GESTURE TO into the answer; the political surface makes 'reform' look like policy.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue state is a nation whose government behaves lawlessly and cannot be relied on.

clue.text: Seize one's time to open sluice

indicators.note: something set to open another is placed inside it, splitting it apart

parts.note: a sluice is a channel for draining water, so a drain
one is I and 's is IS, giving I'S

explanation.surface: Someone takes their turn to open the sluice gate.
explanation.definitionFit: To distrain is a legal term for seizing goods to force payment of a debt.

clue.text: Force to accept a commendation

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: to prise is to force open with a lever

explanation.surface: Someone is pressed into accepting a word of commendation.
explanation.definitionFit: Praise is approval expressed in words, the same thing as a commendation.

clue.text: As unpleasant climax, left to trail Londonwards perhaps

indicators.note: to trail is to follow behind, so this letter comes at the end

parts.note: heading towards London is going to the capital, with 'perhaps' marking London as one example

explanation.surface: Someone trails off towards London as the final unpleasant touch.
explanation.walkthrough: Any capital city would do, hence 'perhaps' after Londonwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom marks the last and worst of a run of misfortunes, a sour climax to them.

clue.text: Louis XIV more than half ruined

indicators.note: keeping more than half of a seven-letter phrase means its first four letters survive, the rest dropped

parts.note: Louis XIV of France was known as the Sun King

explanation.surface: Something belonging to Louis XIV is more than half wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: Louis XIV's nickname, the Sun King, loses its last three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunk as in done for: a plan that is sunk has been ruined beyond rescue.

clue.text: Tree beginning to mature fast

parts.note: the fir is a coniferous tree

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A tree starts to mature quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like speed but means fixed, steadfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Fast in the sense of firmly fixed, as in holding fast or a fast colour.

clue.text: No longer the place for setting out

parts.note: ex means former, no longer the case
a position is a place or spot

explanation.surface: This used to be the spot where things were set out.
explanation.definitionFit: An exposition is a setting out of facts or ideas, a detailed explanation.

clue.text: Some pork: what you'd associate with scratchings on floor

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece set on another follows it

parts.note: an itch is what makes you scratch

explanation.surface: Pork talk: pork scratchings (a British crackling snack) dropped on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: Pork scratchings, fried pork rind sold in British pubs, steer you to crackling, but the scratching is of an itch.
explanation.definitionFit: A flitch is a whole side of bacon, salted and cured, so a cut of pork.

clue.text: Photons don't have any, everything else a large amount

parts.note: the rest is all the remainder
a mass of something is a great quantity

explanation.surface: A physics fact: photons lack it, while everything else has plenty.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one sentence about photons, but 'everything else' is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Physics term for the mass of a body at rest, which for light particles is zero.

clue.text: Who once regularly secured one a rise?

definitions.text: Who once regularly secured one a rise?

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter, here the second and fourth

parts.note: secured means got, obtained
one is the Roman numeral I
a tor is a rocky hill, a rise in the land

explanation.surface: A union official is remembered for having routinely won pay increases.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a union official who in past times regularly won members a pay rise.
explanation.definitionFit: A union bargainer would be the person who argued for and secured pay increases.

clue.text: Stick note into bundle of them

indicators.note: one piece put into another goes inside it

parts.note: a wad is a bundle of banknotes, 'them' pointing back to notes

explanation.surface: Someone pushes a banknote into a fat bundle of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A wand is a slender stick, as carried by a magician or conductor.

clue.text: Scrapping speech may produce challenge

definitions.meaning: talk used in a scrap, that is a fight
provocative words that dare someone to fight

explanation.surface: Aggressive talk can provoke a challenge to fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrapping' means fighting, not discarding.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means provocative or insulting remarks, the sort of speech that invites a fight.

clue.text: Such an army sensitive to trespassers?

definitions.meaning: Britain's volunteer reserve force was called the ... Army
defensive of one's own patch, like an animal guarding its ground

explanation.surface: An army that bristles at anyone crossing its border.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army was the British part-time reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective names the British reserve army and also an animal's urge to defend its own ground.

clue.text: Disprove underground river's rising

indicators.note: in a down answer, rising means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the Tube is the London Underground
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Someone denies that the river is rising up into the underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns TUBER round. The Tube is London's underground railway.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebut an argument is to refute it, showing it to be false.

clue.text: Opera on box including one English standard

parts.note: Norma is Bellini's opera

indicators.note: including means holding something within, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: the box is slang for television, TV
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: An opera broadcast on television becomes a classic English standard.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'on' puts NORMA above the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Normative means relating to a norm or standard, setting what ought to be.

clue.text: Arresting spy, man almost crimson

indicators.note: arresting means seizing and holding, so one piece is held inside another
almost means not quite complete, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent

explanation.surface: A man has almost been caught red-handed arresting a spy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims MAN to MA, which then holds AGENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Magenta is a purplish red, close enough to crimson for crossword use.

clue.text: Sound of poor quality that comes from bird

indicators.note: the sound of a word is how it is heard, giving a word spoken alike

parts.note: cheap means shoddy, of poor quality

explanation.surface: A thin, poor-quality noise issues from a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like the noise itself but signals a word heard alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheep is the shrill little call a young bird makes, the noise coming from it.

clue.text: On the road from inn, artist falling

indicators.note: falling suggests tumbling into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: An artist stumbles out of an inn on a road trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falling' rearranges the letters of INN and ARTIST; 'from' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means travelling, on the way between places, like goods on the road.

clue.text: Amphibian moved off, heading away

indicators.note: a word's heading is its first letter, which goes away

parts.note: left means departed, moved off

explanation.surface: An amphibian moved off, head turned away.
explanation.definitionFit: An eft is a newt, a small amphibian, especially a young one.

clue.text: Finest lyric and book

definitions.meaning: a Hebrew idiom for the best of all songs
a book of the Old Testament, also called the Song of Solomon

explanation.surface: The best poem of all, and a book too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The Biblical book's title is a Hebrew superlative meaning the greatest of lyrics.

clue.text: One who trumpeted he was the Man in the Moon?

definitions.text: he was the Man in the Moon
definitions.meaning: Neil, first person to walk on the Moon in 1969

explanation.surface: A trumpeter is fancifully cast as the man in the moon.
explanation.walkthrough: Two famous people share the surname: a jazz trumpeter and the first moonwalker; the question mark flags the playful twist on the folk figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Both Louis the jazz trumpeter and Neil the astronaut carry this surname.

clue.text: Endure something that sucks, a back-breaking burden

parts.note: to last is to endure, keep going
a drinking straw is sucked through

explanation.surface: Putting up with a vacuum cleaner is the final burden.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says the final straw broke the camel's back.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb's final small load that breaks the camel's back stands for one burden too many.

clue.text: Feeble joke about girl being strait-laced

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: a pun is a weak play on words
Rita is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl doesn't laugh at a weak wordplay joke because she's prim.
explanation.definitionFit: A Puritan, by extension, is anyone strict and prudish in morals.

clue.text: Is the criminal perpetrating this?

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters are bent out of order

explanation.surface: A question of whether the crook is carrying out this crime.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a criminal might well be perpetrating a robbery.
explanation.definitionFit: A heist is a robbery, the kind of crime a criminal perpetrates.

clue.text: Marks debtor, one running across the lawn

parts.note: M is an abbreviation for marks, the old German currency
a debtor is one who owes, an ower

explanation.surface: A debtor called Marks runs across the lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawnmower is pushed back and forth over the grass, running across it.

clue.text: Tiny creature ran off, shortly picked up

indicators.note: in a down answer, picked up means lifted, so the letters read upwards
shortly means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: fled means ran off

explanation.surface: A tiny creature ran away and was soon caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' cuts FLED to FLE, and 'picked up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: An elf is a small sprite from folklore, a tiny magical being.
